text:
The man is likely to prevail. When he acquired the woman's house, he already owned the servient strip, so the easement merged into his fee and was extinguished, and his failure to take possession doesn't change that because merger turns on unity of title, not possession. His later warranty deed could not revive or pass an easement that no longer existed, so the purchaser has no easement and the barricade is likely lawful.

CONFIDENCE: 72
